# Scope verdict on PR #117 vs SFCC-847

**Verdict up front, because it's the consequence that matters most: BOTH.** The PR under-delivers three named facets of its own current AC list (Material, Sleeve Length, Availability aren't wired to anything real — they only exist as decorative Storybook mockups), delivers one AC differently than written (checkboxes standing in for "radio buttons" on Category, twice), and inverts a fourth (the "Selected" chip shows on collapse, not inside the expanded accordion as AC4 says) — while simultaneously shipping a page-level chip-pagination system the PR's own code comment admits belongs to a different, currently-Blocked ticket, rewriting a shared drawer recipe used by three other tickets' components, reworking an unrelated auth button variant, and editing a Tier 1 design-token file with no designer sign-off visible anywhere in the trail. Neither direction is small enough to net out against the other.

Below is the evidence, in the order asked.

## 1. AC-by-AC table

| # | AC (verbatim, shortened) | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Drawer → facet groups display as accordions | **Delivered** | `pr117-head/overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:1355-1372` wires `ZimmDrawer` → `ZimmFiltersDrawerContent`; `pr117-head/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:58-62` renders `ZimmAccordion` with the live `facetGroups`. |
| 2 | Category-PLP(All) → top-level options as **radio buttons** | **Delivered differently than specified** | `product-list/index.tsx:710-727` renders a base Chakra `Checkbox` (imported line 42 from `shared/ui`, not a `Radio`), toggled single-select via `handleCategoryChange`. Behaves like a radio, is not one — see §2. |
| 3 | Category-PLP(Dresses) → sub-category options as **radio buttons** | **Delivered differently than specified** | Same code path — `resolvedCategoryOptions` is generic; there's no separate "Dresses" branch in the shipped page. Same `Checkbox`, same caveat. |
| 4 | variant=Selected → chosen value as chip **inside the expanded accordion**, replacing the list | **Delivered differently than specified** | `zimmAccordion/index.tsx:88-91`: `alwaysVisibleContent` (the chip) renders only `{!isExpanded && ...}`; `content` (the full list) is what `AccordionPanel` shows when expanded. `product-list/index.tsx:692-707`'s own comment: "Selected chips sit in **alwaysVisibleContent** so they are visible **while the accordion is collapsed**. The full checkbox list is in content (**expanded panel only**)." That is the literal inverse of the AC's wording, with no Figma citation reconciling the difference (contrast with the Figma-node citations elsewhere in the same file, e.g. line 52-53, 1366-1367). |
| 5 | Only one accordion expanded at a time | **Delivered** | `zimmAccordion/index.tsx:73` `<Accordion allowToggle ...>` (Chakra default: single-open); asserted in `zimmAccordion/index.stories.tsx`'s `OnlyOneExpandedAtATime` play function. |
| 6 | Expanded → content visible; Collapsed → only label visible | **Delivered** | `zimmAccordion/index.tsx:72-97`; `zimmAccordion/index.test.tsx:29-33` asserts `aria-expanded` true/false per item. |
| 7 | Clicking a header toggles it | **Delivered** | `zimmAccordion/index.stories.tsx`'s `ClickTogglesExpansion` play function (click → `aria-expanded=true` → click → `false`); native Chakra `AccordionButton` behaviour. |
| 8 | Colour → stacked checkbox-group with colour swatches | **Delivered** | `product-list/index.tsx:770-792` routes colour through `ZimmCheckboxGroup`; `zimmCheckboxGroup/index.tsx:30` uses `<Stack>`; `zimmCheckbox/index.tsx:52-60` renders the swatch dot from `cssColorGroups[v.presentationId]`. |
| 9 | Size → three sub-groups (Clothing 0P–4, Accessories S/M/L/One Size, Shoes 36-41) | **Not delivered against real data** | `zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:61-67`'s own docblock: "the API currently returns c_size **flat**, so the ungrouped branch is what renders **today**. Producing the grouped design is **BM configuration**... not a front-end change." The code path exists and is unit-tested with synthetic nested fixtures, but nothing in this PR makes the three real sub-groups appear — that depends on SFCC-104 (see §6). |
| 10 | Availability → two checkboxes: Available, Coming Soon | **Not delivered** | No `Availability`/`Coming Soon` string or special-cased component exists anywhere in `product-list/index.tsx` or any shipped component. The only occurrence is a decorative mock in `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx:105-109` (`☐ Available` / `☐ Coming Soon` as literal `<chakra.li>` text, explicitly labelled in that file's own header comment, lines 17-24, as "a stand-in for the real facet UI SFCC-108 will build"). |
| 11 | Material → stacked checkbox-group | **Not delivered** | Same as above — only `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx:112-120`'s `MaterialPlaceholder` mock exists. Nothing in `product-list/index.tsx` special-cases or guarantees Material renders; it would only appear if/when SFCC returns a `material`-shaped refinement (SFCC-104 dependent). |
| 12 | Sleeve Length → stacked checkbox-group | **Not delivered** | Same pattern — `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx:122-130`'s `SleeveLengthPlaceholder` mock only. |
| 13 | CLEAR (Secondary) + APPLY (Primary), Button-group layout=Inline | **Delivered** | `zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:63-66`: two `ZimmButton`s (`variant="secondary"`/`"primary"`) side by side in a footer row. |
| 14 | WCAG 2.1 AA: accordion label+state, keyboard, CLEAR purposeful label | **Substantially delivered (not independently audited)** | `aria-expanded` confirmed (AC6 evidence); `zimmCheckbox/index.tsx:32` and `zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:30` set `aria-label` via `ADD_FILTER`/`REMOVE_FILTER`; CLEAR's accessible name resolves to the literal string "CLEAR" (`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:64`, `zimmButton/index.tsx:178`) — a real, non-empty label, though not obviously more "purposeful" than the visible text. I did not run an axe/keyboard-trap pass — see unverified gaps. |

## 2. Radio vs checkbox — confirmed from source

The Category facet renders a plain Chakra `Checkbox`, not a `Radio`: `pr117-head/overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:710-727`, using the base `Checkbox` imported at line 42 from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui`. `Radio`/`RadioGroup` are imported (lines 40-41) but never rendered anywhere in this file (confirmed by grep — their only other occurrence is a comment at line 566 about a *different*, unrelated OOTB `RadioRefinement` code path). Single-select is enforced only in JS state (`pendingCategoryId` is a scalar, not an array — `handleCategoryChange`, line 525), not via the native radio-button semantics AC2/AC3 ask for. This is exactly the deviation flagged in Bryan's own unanswered 2026-09-18 comment about switching Category to multi-select checkboxes — except the shipped code is single-select-behaving-as-checkboxes, which is neither the AC's radio-button spec nor Bryan's own proposed multi-select. It is a third, undiscussed state.

## 3. Over-scope — every file/behaviour the ticket didn't ask for

| File/behaviour | (a) necessary plumbing / (b) unrelated | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx:149` | **(b) unrelated** | One-line comment addition (`// shippingAddress is Record<string,unknown>...`), zero logic change, zero connection to filters. Untiered file, but not in this ticket's manifest by any reading. |
| `theme/foundation/colour.ts` (+`grey[150]`), `theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` (+`border-tertiary`) | **(a) necessary value, wrong process — this is the one I'd stop the loop for** | Both files are named, explicitly, in `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`'s Tier 1 list, and AGENTS.md Hard Rule #3 says design-token changes go through the UI designer, full stop. The new token genuinely gets used (`zimmAccordion.css.ts:20-21`'s divider, `product-list/index.tsx:1114,1137`'s bar separator) — so I'm not saying it's decorative churn — but nothing in the commit (`c0da306d fix(filters): correct drawer layout, checkbox spacing, and grey[150] token`) or the code cites a designer sign-off, in a codebase that otherwise consistently cites "Figma-confirmed," "audited," or "PO-approved" for every other new value. This is a Tier 1 file touched without visible authorisation — a hard stop on its own, independent of everything else in this table. |
| `components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` (net -143 lines rewritten), `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` (`hasOverlay` prop) | **Mixed — real fix bundled with wide unrelated collateral** | `hasOverlay` (index.tsx) is harmless, additive, and unused beyond its own default (`product-list/index.tsx:1359` passes `true`, the default) — low-cost, arguably unneeded, not harmful. The recipe rewrite is the problem: it touches **every size variant** (`large`, `tablet`, `small`, `xLarge`, `prompt`, `mobile`), not just the `large` size the new filter drawer actually uses. `large` is also what `ZimmPdpDrawer` renders at `xl` breakpoint (`pages/product-detail/index.tsx:977-980`) — SFCC-736, status **In SIT**. `prompt` belongs to `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch` (SFCC-831, already-approved). `small` belongs to both the PDP "Find in Boutique" drawer and `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (SFCC-742, a different developer's ticket). The rewrite also **reverts** an explicitly-documented, explicitly-approved value: `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE` goes from `80px` back to `72px` (`zimmDrawer.css.ts:57`), undoing a fix the deleted comment says was "approved 2026-09-12 (Wishlist/Login)" after a live Playwright re-measurement — and the new comment re-attributes the reversal to "SFCC-926 (Figma)," a ticket already merged into `develop` *before* this PR branched (confirmed: `6babac68` is an ancestor of the PR base). So a third ticket is being cited to justify undoing a second ticket's signed-off fix, from inside a first ticket's PR, for a size variant that ticket doesn't even use. That's the "different owner, different approver" collision the brief warns about, in concrete form. |
| `components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx` (net +5 lines, but a real internal rewrite) | **Mixed** | Adding `ariaLabel`/`role`/`ariaChecked` to `ZimmLabelButtonProps` (lines 37, 52, 95, 105, 145, 169, 178, 181) is legitimate, minimal plumbing — `ZimmSizeFilter`'s chip buttons need it. Splitting `variant="social"` into its own `ZimmSocialButtonProps` type is a plausible side effect of that. But the *implementation* swap — replacing the recipe-driven `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmSocialButton', ...)` render with hand-rolled inline `React.CSSProperties` (commit `f7607681 fix(zimm-button): use plain span + inline style for social icon box`, no ticket cited) — has nothing to do with filters. `variant="social"` (Apple/Google sign-in) was already shipped on `develop` via SFCC-926 before this branch existed; this PR reopens and re-implements someone else's already-merged auth work. |
| `constants/index.ts` | **Mixed** | The `cssColorGroups` re-export (line ~176) is real, necessary plumbing for AC8's swatches. The full-file reformat of the unrelated `SHIPPING_COUNTRY_CODES` array (all 32 entries, quote/spacing/semicolon style only, no value changes) is pure autoformat noise on a checkout-country constant that has nothing to do with filters. |
| `utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts`, `utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`, `pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` | **(b) unrelated** | Each gets one identical added trailing comment (`// filterImageGroups returns a loose type; cast narrows to the SDK's typed shape`) on a pre-existing type-cast line. No behaviour change, no connection to filters — these are recently-viewed-rail/PLP-card image-selection utilities. |
| Page-level `SelectedChipRow` (CLEAR ALL + windowed chips + prev/next arrows, `product-list/index.tsx:249-316`, plus `chipsPerPage`/`chipOffset` state) | **(b) unrelated, self-admitted** | Nothing in any AC describes a page-level applied-filter chip strip with pagination arrows above the grid. The PR's own comment, `product-list/index.tsx:751-752`, says it outright: **"Applied-filter chip patterns as a page-level surface belong to SFCC-108 AC #6, not this ticket."** This is the PR building acknowledged SFCC-108 territory anyway. |

The PR description's claim of "replaces grid-fixed-width sizing on size chips with flex-wrap minimum-width" does not match what's actually shipped: `zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:19` uses `<SimpleGrid columns={4}>` — a fixed grid, not flex-wrap — per that file's own comment "One flat grid of size chips using the **OOTB fixed** 44px column width." An intermediate commit (`7a0aefca`) did the opposite move ("replace custom flex... with OOTB 4-column SimpleGrid"). The PR description is describing a state the code no longer is in.

## 4. Under-scope — named items missing entirely

- **Material** — no live wiring, only the Storybook mock (`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.stories.tsx:112-120`).
- **Sleeve Length** — same, mock only (lines 122-130).
- **Availability (Available / Coming Soon)** — same, mock only (lines 105-109); no code anywhere special-cases this facet or guarantees those two exact labels.
- **Size's three named sub-groups** — the grouping *logic* exists (`zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:61-88`) but is inert against live data today, by the file's own admission (line 57: "not a front-end change").

All four are named, specific items from the current AC list. None are silently renamed or partially covered elsewhere — they are simply absent from what a shopper would see today.

## 5. Boundary bleed into SFCC-108 / SFCC-736

**Yes, in both directions, unevenly.** The `ZimmFiltersDrawerContent` organism itself is correctly scoped — it takes `content: React.ReactNode` per facet and its own docblock (`zimmFiltersDrawerContent/index.tsx:9-14, 32-39`) is explicit that facet content is SFCC-108's job. But the actual **application wiring** in `product-list/index.tsx` does not stop at that boundary: it builds real, live-data-driven facet content itself — the Category checkbox list (lines 708-729), the colour-swatch checkbox group (lines 770-792), the size chip grid (line 771) — i.e. exactly the "radio buttons, colour swatches, size options etc." the ticket description assigns to SFCC-108. Since SFCC-108 is **Blocked**, this PR is shipping a working first draft of blocked work under cover of SFCC-847, while simultaneously not finishing the parts of that same content (Material/Sleeve/Availability/Size-grouping) that would make SFCC-108 actually closeable. The page-level chip-pagination system (§3) is the same pattern one level up, and is the one instance the PR's own comments concede outright.

I did not find any code that touches `ZimmDrawer`'s shell/overlay/slide-in/close-trigger behaviour itself (SFCC-736's actual scope) beyond the additive `hasOverlay` prop — the boundary bleed there is entirely at the CSS-recipe level described in §3, not a behavioural takeover of SFCC-736's job.

## 6. Blocker — does this depend on SFCC-104 (BM config, still Blocked)?

Partially, and the code is honest about exactly where. `grep -rn "c_categoryIds" overrides/` (searched the whole `overrides/` tree in the head worktree) returns **nothing** — Bryan's proposed new custom attribute was never actually implemented, so the shipped code does not depend on an unbuilt BM attribute for Category. Two hardcoded attribute IDs exist — `COLOR_REFINEMENT_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'c_refinementColor'` and `SIZE_REFINEMENT_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'c_size'` (`product-list/index.tsx:164,168`) — but these only route an *already-existing* refinement to a specific widget (swatch dot vs. size grid); they don't fabricate data SFCC doesn't already return. The real SFCC-104 dependency is narrower and self-documented: **Size's three sub-groups** and, most likely, **Material/Sleeve Length/Availability existing as facets at all** need BM-side refinement configuration that doesn't exist yet (`zimmSizeFilter/index.tsx:57`: "Producing the grouped design is BM configuration... not a front-end change"). So: yes, part of the visible under-delivery in §4 traces directly back to the still-Blocked SFCC-104, not to missed front-end work — but that's exactly why those items should be named as open/blocked in the ticket rather than left silent.

## Required unverified-gaps section

- I did not run the app, Storybook, or a screen reader/axe pass — the WCAG line in the AC table is based on static code reading (aria attributes present in source), not a live audit.
- I did not check the actual Zimmermann Design System 2026 Figma file against any of the node-number citations in the code (e.g. `40003890:151742`, `40007982:184470`) — I'm taking those citations at face value from the comments.
- I did not check whether SFCC-104's Business Manager sandboxes currently have *any* refinement data for material/sleeve-length/availability — I'm relying on the code's own comments that this is BM-configuration-gated, not a direct BM query.
- I have not read PR #117's actual review thread/CI status (CodeRabbit findings, human approvals) beyond the ticket comment thread given to me — commit messages reference two rounds of CodeRabbit fixes already applied, but I didn't independently verify what those covered.

## What Marcel is missing

The Jira automation comment on 2026-09-16 says the story's DoR checklist failed and the issue was auto-moved back — and this PR was opened roughly an hour later, against a story Jira itself had just flagged as not ready. That sequencing (not the diff) is probably why so much of this PR reads like it's improvising scope decisions (the radio→checkbox swap, the inverted Selected-chip placement, the SFCC-108-shaped page chip strip) rather than working from a settled brief — worth checking whether the DoR gate was actually resolved before this PR is merged, independent of anything in the diff itself.
